content: It is important to follow your doctor’s instructions carefully when taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication in its original container at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs. Common side effects may include diarrhea, headache, dizziness, trouble sleeping, unusual dreams, back pain, or changes in the color of the skin on your palms or soles. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing symptoms of those infections to reappear. In some cases, an overactive immune response may occur, which can happen shortly after starting HIV treatment or even months later. Rarely, this medication may cause severe, potentially fatal liver and blood problems, such as lactic acidosis. Tenofovir, one of the components, may increase the risk of bone loss. Discuss the risks and benefits of treatment with your doctor, including the potential use of calcium and vitamin D to mitigate this side effect. If you are at risk for bone loss, your doctor may monitor your bone mineral density. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, this is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, or tenofovir, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can worsen this effect. Avoid driving, using machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication is not recommended for use during pregnancy, as it may not work effectively in pregnant women. If you become pregnant or suspect you may be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. Emtricitabine and tenofovir can pass into breast milk, but it is unknown if elvitegravir or cobicistat do. Discuss breastfeeding with your doctor. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Do not take this medication with other HIV medications, such as ritonavir. This medication can slow the removal of other drugs from your body, potentially affecting how they work. Similarly, other medications can affect the removal of this drug from your body, altering its effectiveness. Examples include mitotane and rifampin. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. It may also increase the risk of certain side effects associated with hormonal birth control. Discuss alternative reliable forms of birth control with your doctor, and use an effective barrier method (such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams) during sexual activity to reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and medical tests, such as kidney and liver function tests, hepatitis B virus testing, viral load, T-cell counts, blood mineral levels, bone density tests, and urine glucose/protein tests, should be conducted before starting this medication and periodically while taking it. For formulary information, create a list of plans to compare the status of this drug with others in the same class. Contact the applicable plan provider for the most current information.
